title: NAV
shortDefinition: Net Asset Value — the per-unit price of a mutual fund scheme.
whyItMatters: When you buy MF units, you pay the day's NAV. It moves daily with the market value of the fund's holdings.
example: If NAV is ₹50 and you invest ₹5,000, you get roughly 100 units (minus any charges).

title: Expense ratio (TER)
shortDefinition: Annual fee the fund charges, expressed as a % of assets — includes management and operating costs.
whyItMatters: A 1.5% expense ratio on ₹10L costs you ₹15,000 every year whether the market rises or falls. Direct plans are cheaper than regular.
example: Index funds often charge 0.1–0.3%; active large-cap funds may charge 1–1.5%.

title: SIP
shortDefinition: Systematic Investment Plan — fixed amount invested automatically on a schedule (usually monthly).
whyItMatters: Removes the need to time the market. You buy more units when NAV is low and fewer when high — rupee-cost averaging.
example: ₹10,000 on the 5th of every month into a Nifty index fund is a SIP.

title: SWP
shortDefinition: Systematic Withdrawal Plan — redeem a fixed amount from your MF holdings on a schedule.
whyItMatters: Used in retirement to draw income while the rest stays invested. Opposite of SIP.
example: Withdraw ₹20,000/month from your debt fund corpus after age 60.

title: Folio number
shortDefinition: Unique account number AMC assigns to your investment in their schemes.
whyItMatters: One folio can hold multiple schemes from the same AMC. Needed for CAS, KYC updates, and nominations.
example: Your HDFC folio might hold both an equity and a debt fund under one number.

title: AMC
shortDefinition: Asset Management Company — the company that runs a mutual fund (e.g. HDFC MF, SBI MF, Parag Parikh MF).
whyItMatters: You don't buy from NSE directly for MFs — you buy units from an AMC (via broker or app).
example: SBI Mutual Fund is the AMC; SBI Bluechip is one of its schemes.

title: RTA (CAMS / KFintech)
shortDefinition: Registrar and Transfer Agent — maintains MF investor records. CAMS and KFintech are the two main RTAs in India.
whyItMatters: Your CAS statement comes from RTAs. They hold folio data across AMCs they service.
example: Request CAS from camsonline.com or rt.kfintech.com to see all MFs in one PDF.

title: Cut-off time
shortDefinition: Deadline by which your MF order must be received to get that day's NAV (or next business day's).
whyItMatters: Submitting after cut-off means a different NAV — matters for large lump sums and volatile days.
example: Equity funds: typically 3 pm on working days. Liquid funds often have later cut-offs.

title: Direct plan
shortDefinition: MF plan bought without a distributor — lower expense ratio, no commission embedded.
whyItMatters: Same scheme as regular plan, same portfolio — you keep ~0.5–1% more per year via lower TER.
example: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Direct vs Regular — same stocks, different expense ratio.

title: Regular plan
shortDefinition: MF plan sold through a distributor who earns trail commission from the fund — higher expense ratio.
whyItMatters: Convenient if an advisor adds value; expensive if you never get advice. Many apps default to direct now.
example: Regular plan TER might be 1.2% vs 0.8% for direct on the same scheme.

title: AUM
shortDefinition: Assets Under Management — total money invested in a fund scheme.
whyItMatters: Very small AUM can mean closure risk; very huge AUM can make it harder for a small-cap fund to manoeuvre.
example: A ₹500 crore small-cap fund behaves differently from a ₹20,000 crore large-cap fund.

title: Exit load
shortDefinition: Penalty fee charged if you redeem MF units before a minimum holding period.
whyItMatters: Protects long-term investors from costs of others churning. Check scheme document before redeeming early.
example: 1% exit load if redeemed within 1 year is common on equity funds.

title: Demat account
shortDefinition: Account that holds shares and ETFs in electronic form — linked to your PAN.
whyItMatters: Mandatory for stocks and ETFs. Different from trading account (orders) but usually opened together.
example: Zerodha demat holds your Reliance shares; trading account places buy/sell orders.

title: ISIN
shortDefinition: International Securities Identification Number — 12-character unique ID for a stock, bond, or MF scheme.
whyItMatters: Used in CAS, tax reports, and to avoid buying the wrong similarly named security.
example: INE002A01018 is Reliance Industries' ISIN.

title: Market order
shortDefinition: Buy or sell immediately at the best available price right now.
whyItMatters: Fast fill but price can slip on volatile stocks — you might pay more than the last traded price shown.
example: Market buy at 10:15 am during a sharp rally — your fill could be above what you saw on screen.

title: Limit order
shortDefinition: Buy or sell only at your specified price or better — may not execute if price never reaches it.
whyItMatters: Control over price; risk of missing the trade if the stock runs away.
example: Limit buy HDFC Bank at ₹1,650 — fills only if price hits ₹1,650 or lower.

title: Bid–ask spread
shortDefinition: Bid = highest price buyers offer; Ask = lowest price sellers want. The gap is the spread.
whyItMatters: Wide spread on illiquid stocks costs you on entry and exit. Large caps usually have tight spreads.
example: Bid ₹100 / Ask ₹100.05 — you buy at ask, sell at bid — instant ₹0.05 loss per share.

title: Circuit limit
shortDefinition: Exchange-imposed daily price band — stock cannot move beyond ±X% in one session (varies by stock).
whyItMatters: Halts extreme moves. If a stock hits upper circuit, sellers disappear — you can't buy until it opens.
example: A 20% circuit on a small cap means max up/down move that day is capped.

title: Intraday
shortDefinition: Buy and sell the same stock within the same trading day — no overnight holding.
whyItMatters: Requires margin; high risk; treated as speculation not investing. Not where beginners should start.
example: Buy Infosys at 10 am, sell at 2 pm — square off same day or broker auto-squares.

title: Delivery (CNC)
shortDefinition: Buy shares and hold them in demat — settlement T+1, you own the stock.
whyItMatters: How long-term investing works. Cash and Carry (CNC) on Zerodha = delivery mode.
example: Buy 10 shares of ITC on delivery — they sit in demat until you sell.

title: F&O (Futures & Options)
shortDefinition: Derivatives contracts on indices or stocks — bet on future price with leverage.
whyItMatters: SEBI data: most retail F&O traders lose money. Requires margin; losses can exceed premium on some strategies.
example: Nifty futures, Bank Nifty options — not the same as buying Nifty ETF.

title: Margin
shortDefinition: Borrowed money or collateral broker lets you trade with — amplifies gains and losses.
whyItMatters: MTF and F&O use margin. A 20% move against you can wipe out 100% of your capital.
example: ₹1L capital + ₹4L margin = ₹5L exposure — a 10% fall hits ₹50k (half your capital).

title: P/E ratio
shortDefinition: Price ÷ Earnings per share — how many years of current profit you'd pay for the stock price.
whyItMatters: High P/E can mean growth expectations or overpricing. Compare within same sector, not across unlike businesses.
example: P/E of 40 vs sector average 25 — market expects faster earnings growth or it's expensive.

title: EPS
shortDefinition: Earnings Per Share — company's net profit divided by number of shares.
whyItMatters: Rising EPS over years often drives stock prices. Check if growth is real or one-off.
example: EPS ₹50 last year → ₹60 this year — 20% earnings growth if share count unchanged.

title: Dividend yield
shortDefinition: Annual dividend per share ÷ share price — cash income as % of price.
whyItMatters: High yield can be a value trap if the business is shrinking. Growth stocks often yield 0%.
example: ₹20 dividend on ₹400 stock = 5% yield.

title: XIRR
shortDefinition: Extended Internal Rate of Return — annualised return accounting for irregular cashflows (SIPs, redemptions).
whyItMatters: The right metric for SIP portfolios. Absolute return misleads when money came in at different times.
example: SIP ₹10k/month for 3 years — XIRR tells your true annualised performance vs a lump sum.

title: CAGR
shortDefinition: Compound Annual Growth Rate — smoothed annual return between two points in time.
whyItMatters: Good for lump sums over fixed periods. '15% CAGR over 5 years' is easier to compare than total return.
example: ₹1L → ₹2L in 5 years ≈ 14.9% CAGR.

title: Drawdown
shortDefinition: Peak-to-trough fall before recovering — measures worst pain period.
whyItMatters: A fund with 15% CAGR but 50% drawdown may be unbearable if you panic-sell at the bottom.
example: Nifty fell ~38% in March 2020 — your portfolio's max drawdown that year matters for sleep test.

title: Alpha
shortDefinition: Return above what you'd expect from benchmark risk — 'did the manager add skill?'
whyItMatters: Positive alpha after fees is hard to sustain. Most active funds fail long-term vs index.
example: Fund returned 14%, Nifty 12% — rough alpha ≈ 2% (simplified; beta matters too).

title: Beta
shortDefinition: Sensitivity to market moves — beta 1.0 moves with index; 1.5 moves 50% more.
whyItMatters: High-beta funds amplify both rallies and crashes. Match beta to your risk appetite.
example: Beta 0.5 debt-heavy hybrid — calmer than Nifty in downturns.

title: Sharpe ratio
shortDefinition: Return earned per unit of total risk (volatility) — higher is better risk-adjusted performance.
whyItMatters: Compares funds on risk-adjusted basis, not raw return alone.
example: Two funds both 12% return — Sharpe 0.8 vs 0.5 means first took less volatility per unit of return.

title: NSE
shortDefinition: National Stock Exchange — India's largest stock exchange by volume (Mumbai).
whyItMatters: Most liquid stocks trade heavily on NSE. Nifty 50 is NSE's flagship index.
example: Reliance trades on NSE as RELIANCE with ticker you search on broker apps.

title: BSE
shortDefinition: Bombay Stock Exchange — Asia's oldest exchange; Sensex tracks 30 BSE stocks.
whyItMatters: Same company can list on both NSE and BSE — usually pick one for liquidity.
example: Sensex 30 vs Nifty 50 — different index compositions.

title: Nifty 50
shortDefinition: Index of 50 large NSE-listed companies — shorthand for 'how big Indian stocks did'.
whyItMatters: Benchmark for most large-cap funds. Nifty index funds aim to match its return minus fees.
example: TV says 'Nifty up 200 points' — means the index rose, not that every stock you own did.

title: T+1 settlement
shortDefinition: Trade day + 1 working day — when shares or cash actually exchange hands after your order.
whyItMatters: India moved to T+1 for equities — faster than old T+2. Affects when you can sell what you bought.
example: Buy Monday → shares in demat Tuesday (typically).

title: KYC
shortDefinition: Know Your Customer — one-time identity verification (PAN, Aadhaar, photo) required to invest in India.
whyItMatters: SEBI mandate. Without valid KYC you cannot buy MFs or open demat. Update on address change.
example: Complete e-KYC on CAMS or broker app in ~10 minutes.

title: PAN
shortDefinition: Permanent Account Number — 10-character tax ID mandatory for all investments in India.
whyItMatters: Links all your financial activity to one ID — MFs, stocks, FD interest, ITR.
example: ABCDE1234F format — on your PAN card.

title: CAS (Consolidated Account Statement)
shortDefinition: Single statement listing MF holdings across AMCs — from CAMS or KFintech.
whyItMatters: See entire MF portfolio in one PDF. Essential for overlap analysis and tax reporting.
example: Request monthly CAS to email — free from RTA websites.

title: STT
shortDefinition: Securities Transaction Tax — small tax on each buy/sell of stocks, ETFs, F&O on Indian exchanges.
whyItMatters: Built into trading costs. Equity delivery STT differs from intraday and F&O rates.
example: Charged automatically by broker on each trade — shows on contract note.

title: SEBI
shortDefinition: Securities and Exchange Board of India — market regulator protecting investors and overseeing brokers, MFs.
whyItMatters: Registers brokers, mandates disclosures, studies retail F&O losses. Not a guarantee against fraud — due diligence still yours.
example: Check broker is SEBI-registered before transferring money.

title: STCG
shortDefinition: Short-Term Capital Gains — profit tax when you sell before the long-term holding period.
whyItMatters: Equity STCG (held <1 year) taxed at 20% (post 2024 rules — verify current slab). Debt rules differ.
example: Sell MF units 8 months after buying — gains may be STCG not LTCG.

title: LTCG
shortDefinition: Long-Term Capital Gains — profit tax when you sell after holding beyond the defined period.
whyItMatters: Equity LTCG above ₹1.25L/year taxed at 12.5% (verify current rules). Holding period matters for tax planning.
example: Hold equity MF >1 year before redeeming large gains — different tax treatment.

title: ELSS
shortDefinition: Equity Linked Savings Scheme — tax-saving MF with 3-year lock-in under Section 80C.
whyItMatters: Only MF category with 80C benefit. Must stay locked 3 years — not an emergency fund.
example: ₹1.5L in ELSS → deduction under 80C + equity exposure (with lock-in).

title: Section 80C
shortDefinition: IT Act section allowing up to ₹1.5 lakh/year deduction via PPF, ELSS, EPF, life insurance premium, etc.
whyItMatters: Reduces taxable income, not tax on returns. Choose instruments that fit goal — don't buy junk insurance for 80C alone.
example: ₹1.5L across PPF + ELSS + EPF premiums in one financial year.

title: Indexation
shortDefinition: Adjusting purchase price for inflation before calculating capital gains — mainly on debt/gold/long-term assets.
whyItMatters: Lowers taxable gain when inflation was high. Not available on equity LTCG the same way.
example: Buy debt fund units, sell after 3 years — indexed cost reduces tax vs nominal gain.

title: TDS on investments
shortDefinition: Tax Deducted at Source — payer deducts tax before paying you (FD interest, dividends in some cases).
whyItMatters: TDS ≠ final tax. You may owe more or get refund after filing ITR depending on slab.
example: Bank deducts 10% TDS on FD interest above threshold — claim credit in ITR.

title: YTM
shortDefinition: Yield to Maturity — total return you'd earn holding a bond/debt instrument till maturity.
whyItMatters: Better compare debt funds and bonds than coupon rate alone — includes price moves.
example: Bond trading at discount with 7% coupon might have YTM of 8%.

title: Credit rating
shortDefinition: Agency score (AAA, AA, etc.) of issuer's ability to repay — CRISIL, ICRA, CARE in India.
whyItMatters: Higher rating = lower default risk, usually lower yield. Never chase yield without checking rating.
example: AAA corporate bond vs BBB — very different risk despite yield gap.

title: Sum assured
shortDefinition: Guaranteed payout amount on term insurance if the insured event happens — not an investment return.
whyItMatters: Term insurance = pure protection. Sum assured should cover 10–15× annual income for dependents.
example: ₹1 crore term plan — family gets ₹1Cr on valid claim, no maturity value if you survive.

title: Insurance premium
shortDefinition: Amount you pay for insurance coverage — term, health, ULIP. Not the same as investment SIP.
whyItMatters: Term premium buys protection only. ULIP premium mixes insurance + investment — usually expensive vs separate term + MF.
example: ₹15k/year term premium for ₹1Cr cover vs ₹15k/month MF SIP — different jobs.

title: Liquid fund
shortDefinition: Debt MF investing in very short-term money-market instruments — high liquidity, low risk.
whyItMatters: Parking emergency fund alternative to savings account — not guaranteed like FD but usually stable.
example: Redeem T+1; used for 3–6 month expense buffer.

title: Gilt fund
shortDefinition: Debt MF investing mainly in government securities — low credit risk, rate-sensitive.
whyItMatters: When interest rates fall, gilt NAVs often rise — and vice versa. Not 'safe' from volatility.
example: Long-duration gilt funds can swing 5–10% in a year despite holding govt bonds.

title: IPO
shortDefinition: Initial Public Offering — first time a company sells shares to the public on NSE/BSE.
whyItMatters: Hype ≠ returns. Many IPOs list above fair value and fall later. Read red herring prospectus.
example: Apply via UPI in broker app; may get partial allotment if oversubscribed.

title: ETF
shortDefinition: Exchange Traded Fund — basket of assets (e.g. Nifty 50) that trades on exchange like a stock.
whyItMatters: Low cost index exposure; needs demat; price can differ slightly from NAV (tracking error + spread).
example: Nifty BeES — buy on NSE like a share, holds Nifty 50 stocks.

title: Index fund
shortDefinition: MF that passively tracks an index (Nifty, Sensex) — low TER, no stock-picking manager.
whyItMatters: Beats most active funds over 10+ years after fees. Default recommendation for equity beginners.
example: UTI Nifty Index Fund mirrors Nifty 50 composition.

title: Rebalancing
shortDefinition: Bringing portfolio back to target allocation by selling overweight assets and buying underweight.
whyItMatters: Disciplined way to 'buy low sell high' without predicting markets. Usually annual or on drift thresholds.
example: Equity grew from 50% to 65% of portfolio — sell some equity, add debt to restore 50/50 target.
